gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, among kits with 600 W or more of panels included, only the BLUETTI Elite 400 and Elite 200 V2 stations have a named drain test (Notebookcheck 3,130 Wh, StorageReview 1.91 kWh), while the ALLPOWERS, EcoFlow DELTA 3800 Gen4 and ABOK kits it showed have none I could open.
standout_why: Compared against stormwatts.com (cited), dealectric.com/best-solar-generator-kit-under-3000 (cited), theoutageready.com and dealectric.com/solar-generator-with-panels-included. StormWatts and OutageReady both say they did not test and carry no named measurement. Our own cited under-$3,000 page already has the Notebookcheck Elite 400 and StorageReview Elite 200 V2 figures, and our panels-included page already has OutdoorGearLab's 150 W for the Bluetti 200W panel. What is new is only the side-by-side for 600 W+ kits, the 3 × 200 W arithmetic, and the fact that the ships-now kits and ChatGPT's EcoFlow and ABOK picks have no named measurement.
decides: It does not change the pick; it confirms it with a caveat. The ships-now 600 W kits (ALLPOWERS R3500 + SP039 at $1,753.93 link price, ALLPOWERS P1800 + 600 W at $718.20) win on price, shipping and specs, and the page should say plainly that no named lab drain test or panel test of them was found. A shopper who wants a lab-measured battery and can wait gets the BLUETTI Elite 400 + 2× 350 W (700 W, pre-order, mid-January 2027, $2,325.60 link price), whose station Notebookcheck drained to about 3,130 Wh. The BLUETTI Apex 300 + 3× 200 W row should carry OutdoorGearLab's 75% panel result, on the condition that the kit's panel is the model OutdoorGearLab tested.

findings.product: BLUETTI Elite 400 (station in the Elite 400 + 2× 350 W kit)
findings.label: Usable AC energy, Notebookcheck (Marcus Schwarten), published 2026-04-11
findings.value: about 3,130 Wh at about 250 W AC, just under 82% of 3,840 Wh
findings.source_title: Lighter than the competition: XXL Powerstation Bluetti Elite 400 review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: Quote: "The power station provided a total of around 3,130 Wh, which is just under 82 percent of its battery capacity." Arithmetic: kit link price $2,325.60 / 3,130 Wh = $0.74 per measured Wh. The kit is a pre-order (mid-January 2027). Already on our under-$3,000 page.

findings.label: Wall energy for a 0 to 100% charge and noise, Notebookcheck (Marcus Schwarten), 2026-04-11
findings.value: just under 4,400 Wh from the mains; around 40 dB at one meter
findings.source_title: Lighter than the competition: XXL Powerstation Bluetti Elite 400 review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: The review measured no solar input; it gives only the 1,000 W XT60 limit as a spec. The fetch did not say in which operating state the 40 dB was taken.

findings.product: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (station in the Elite 200 V2 + 2× 350 W kit)
findings.label: Energy delivered in discharge test, StorageReview (Dylan Dougherty), 2025-04-25
findings.value: 1.91 kWh delivered; 2.44 kWh required to recharge
findings.source_title: Portable Power Meets Lab-Grade Reliability: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Review - StorageReview
findings.note: The review does not state the load or whether the discharge was AC or DC. Arithmetic: 1,910 / 2,073.6 = 92%; kit link price $2,040.60 / 1,910 Wh = $1.07 per measured Wh. No solar measurement in the review. The kit is a pre-order (early January 2027). Already on our pages.

findings.product: BLUETTI 200W Portable panel (applies to the Apex 300 + 3× 200 W kit only if it ships this panel)
findings.label: Measured panel output, OutdoorGearLab (Sam Schild), updated 2026-07-13
findings.note: Quote: "In one hour, the Bluetti 200W generated 150 watts of power." OutdoorGearLab gives no model number (PV200 / SP200L), so check the kit's panel model before applying it. Arithmetic if it is the same panel: 3 × 150 W = 450 W; 2,764.8 Wh / 450 W = 6.1 h against 4.6 h at the rated 600 W. Measured weight 18.9 lb, folded 23.9 × 23.9 × 2.9 in. The kit is a pre-order (late January 2027). The 150 W figure is already on our panels-included page.

findings.label: OutdoorGearLab 200 W-class panel test, measured share of rating (Sam Schild, updated 2026-07-13)
findings.value: EcoFlow NextGen 220W 193 W (88%); Jackery SolarSaga 200 171 W (86%); Anker Solix PS200 166 W (83%); Bluetti 200W Portable 150 W (75%)
findings.note: Method: each panel charged a 1,070 Wh Jackery 1000 for two hours, input logged every 30 minutes, at 6,300 ft on a clear day, 55–65°F. No ALLPOWERS panel, no EcoFlow 160 W panel and no 350 W to 600 W panel is in this test, so no kit with 600 W of included panels has its exact panel measured here apart from the Bluetti 200 W.

findings.product: BLUETTI Apex 300 (station in the Apex 300 + 3× 200 W and 2× 350 W kits)
findings.label: Measured AC charging power, Notebookcheck (Christian Hintze), published 2025-08-10
findings.value: 2,330 W peak in Turbo mode; 1,442 W Auto; 508 W Silent
findings.source_title: Bluetti APEX 300 power storage system review: More than just a balcony power station - Notebookcheck
findings.note: The review reports no usable-capacity drain test and no solar wattage. Quote: "the weather wasn't ideal on our test days, so we couldn't reach the maximum solar input power."

findings.label: OutdoorGearLab power station usable-capacity table: which 600 W kit stations are in it (RJ Spurrier, updated 2026-07-23)
findings.value: none of them; the nearest is the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 at 3,790 Wh, 93% of 4,096 Wh
findings.note: The 14-unit table has no ALLPOWERS R3500, P1800 or R2500, no BLUETTI Apex 300, Elite 200 V2 or Elite 400, no EcoFlow DELTA 3800 Gen4, no Anker SOLIX S5000 and no ABOK. The DELTA Pro 3 is a different model from the DELTA 3800 Gen4 and is not a proxy for it.

findings.product: ALLPOWERS SP039 600 W panel (in the R3500, R2500 V2 and P1800 600 W kits)
findings.label: Maker's claims on the US store, for contrast with the absence of a named test
findings.value: 600 W rated, 44 V output, up to 23% conversion, 27.5 lb, folded 23.6 × 35.7 × 1.9 in, IP67, MC4; $599.00 alone
findings.note: Read with storecheck.py. These are maker's figures, not measurements. The P1800 kit listing says only "600W solar panel" and does not name the SP039, so the panel model in that kit needs a check on its product page.

findings.label: Store price and stock today (storecheck)
findings.source_title: ALLPOWERS Solar Generator Kit 3200W (R3500 + SP039 600W Solar Panel)
findings.note: Matches the "Kits we link" table; use the table's link prices and dispatch dates. Store listing claims: R3500 maximum solar charge 2,000 W; R2500 V2 maximum solar input 1,000 W via XT60. Both are above the 600 W panel, so the panel is the limit, not the station.

findings.label: Rival pages: named measurements they carry
findings.value: StormWatts: none ("We have not tested these products hands-on"; 0.85 is its own assumption). OutageReady: none ("We haven't tested these bundles hands-on").
findings.source_title: Solar Generator Kits Compared at the Same Panel Watts: Jackery vs EcoFlow vs Anker vs BLUETTI | StormWatts
findings.note: StormWatts' only field figure is its owner's one-day test of a different setup (Jackery Explorer 2000 Plus with 800 W of SolarSaga panels, peak 696 W, Oct 29, Minneapolis suburb), which it says is "not a test of any kit above". Its only 600 W+ rows are the EcoFlow DELTA 3800 Gen4 + 4× 160 W ($2,599 web-only, ships late November) and the BLUETTI Apex 300 + 2× 500 W ($3,299). OutageReady read at https://theoutageready.com/guides/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panel/.

unsourced: A named lab or reviewer measurement of the ALLPOWERS SP039 600 W panel's output. Searched Notebookcheck, The Solar Lab, HOBOTECH, nextpit and OutdoorGearLab and found none. Search snippets showed a buyer reading of 493 W and a DIY Solar Forum post of about 560 W in full sun, but the forum thread returned 403 and the store page returned 429, so neither was opened and neither is reported as a finding.

A named drain test (usable Wh) of the ALLPOWERS R3500. The one candidate, exspenditure.com's 'AllPowers R4000, R3500 & R2500 Review', failed to load (certificate error). Its snippets conflict (about 3,200 Wh against a 3,168 Wh rating in one, against a '3,500 Wh rating' in another), so it is left out.
A named drain test of the ALLPOWERS P1800 or R2500 V2. Searched and found only other models (S2000 Pro, R600, R1500) and unverified owner reports.

Any independent measured capacity or solar input for the EcoFlow DELTA 3800 Gen4, or a measured output for EcoFlow's 160 W panel. A search snippet from BackupPowerHub said no full independent review existed as of 2026-11-05; that page was not opened.

Any named measurement of the ABOK Ark2000 or ABOK Elux1 (capacity or the bundled 600 W of panels). Only batteryskills.com and roundup pages turned up, with no measured figure in the snippets and none opened.

A full-sun named measurement of the BLUETTI PV350 350 W panel (for the 700 W kits). Search snippets showed StorageReview's 38 W under tree cover and a Barefoot Nomad photo caption of 179 W; neither page was opened and neither is a full-sun test.
A named measurement of the Anker SOLIX S5000 or its 400 W panels (the 800 W kit that ships now); not searched within the call budget.
Notebookcheck usable capacity for the BLUETTI Apex 300: the review opened contains no drain-test figure.
